questions.explain: Bigger props mean higher g/W, which means a longer hover.

questions.q: At what throttle should the drone hover according to the thrust table?
questions.explain: Headroom for wind and maneuvers at a current no higher than ~40% of the continuous rating.

questions.q: ESC continuous current relative to the motor's maximum current:
options: Half as much, the ESC can take short bursts
questions.explain: Margin in current and voltage is the norm.

questions.q: What happens if you keep increasing the battery for flight time?
options: The current drops because the battery is more powerful
questions.explain: Heavier battery → higher current; if it doesn't converge, change the aircraft class.

questions.q: Why does spare part availability matter?
questions.explain: The first repair will show it: an arm you can't buy means the drone sits on the ground.

questions.q: What margin in current and thrust does the module recommend?
questions.explain: A 20% margin pays for itself on the first windy day.

questions.q: Why are cheap components not always a saving?
options: They're heavier: mass means flight time and current
questions.explain: The price/mass trade-off: extra grams cost minutes of flight and amps.
